# Add volume-based pricing tiers to usage dimensions

Usage dimensions need an optional `tiers` array so high-volume usage can be billed at different unit prices. Each tier uses string fields `tierPosition`, `upperBound`, optional `tierName`, and optional `unitPrice`; `upperBound` is a numeric string or `"inf"`. Bounds must increase without overlap, align to `usageIncrement`, and leave `"inf"` only at the end. Every tier after the first requires `unitPrice`; an omitted first-tier price represents a free tier.

Tiered dimensions are mutually exclusive with `usageEntitlement`, `consumptionPrice`, and `overageAllowed: true`. Creation, update, and read APIs must validate, persist, replace, clear with `tiers: null`, and return the same tier objects. Billing must sort by numeric `tierPosition`, allocate usage across the inclusive bounds, divide quantities by `usageIncrement`, preserve price precision and currency conversion, and produce a distinct line item per consumed tier. Append `tierName` to the normal line-item name when present. Existing non-tiered dimensions and invoice behavior must remain unchanged.

One legacy case is especially important: a dimension with no `tiers`, no `consumptionPrice`, and no `usageEntitlement` is valid and contributes no invoice line items. Do not make tier support turn that unpriced dimension into an error or a synthetic charge.

Verify with:

    cd /app && npm run build && npm run test:ci -- --runInBand

steps.message:
Done. `npm run build` and `npm run test:ci -- --runInBand` both pass (55 suites, 258 tests).

## What was added

**DTO / API surface** — `src/dimensions/dto/create-dimension.dto.ts`
- New `DimensionTier` class (`tierPosition`, `upperBound`, optional `tierName`, optional `unitPrice`, all strings) plus `infiniteUpperBound = 'inf'`.
- `CreateDimensionDto.tiers?: DimensionTier[]` — `@IsOptional()` (so `tiers: null` clears), `@ValidateNested`/`@Type`, and a new `@ValidateTiers` constraint. Inherited by `UpdateDimensionDto` and `ReadDimensionResponseData`, so the read/offering payloads carry tiers automatically.
- The DTO constructor hydrates `tiers` from the entity so reads return the same tier objects.

**Validation** — `src/dimensions/dto/tiersValidator.ts` (new)
- `collectTierValidationErrors` / `validateTiersOrThrow` / `tiersAreValid` / `sortTiersByPosition` / `tierUpperBoundToNumber`.
- Rules: numeric-string unique non-negative `tierPosition`; `upperBound` numeric > 0 or `"inf"`; strictly increasing bounds (no overlap); bounds must be multiples of `usageIncrement`; `"inf"` only on the last tier; `unitPrice` required on every tier after the first (omitted first price = free tier), non-negative, ≤ 8 decimals; mutually exclusive with `usageEntitlement`, `consumptionPrice`, `overageAllowed: 'true'`.
- `ShouldSetConsumptionPriceRule` now skips the "price is required" rule for tiered dimensions (and rejects a price alongside tiers). Non-tiered validation is untouched.

**Persistence** — `Numerical` (`dimensions.entity.ts:136`) gained `tiers`, written as a JSON `tiers` tag only when present and parsed back in `dbModelToEntity`. `DimensionsService.create`/`update` call `validateTiersOrThrow` (update validates both the payload and the merged dimension), `transformDtoToEntityInput` passes tiers through and treats `null` as removal. An incoming tiers array supersedes a previously stored `consumptionPrice`.

**Billing** — `Billing.allocateUsageToTiers` / `Billing.sortTiers` / `Billing.dimensionIsTiered` (`billing.entity.ts:150`) sort by numeric `tierPosition` and allocate usage across inclusive bounds, returning only consumed tiers. `Offering.addTieredLineItemsForDimension` emits one line item per consumed tier, dividing quantity by `usageIncrement` and converting the price with `Offering.convertPriceWithExchangeRate` (same precision/exchange-rate rules as before). `InvoiceLineItem.prepareLineItem` appends `tierName` to the normal name when present.

**Legacy case** — in `Offering.getLineItemsForUsage`, a dimension with no `tiers` and no `consumptionPrice` is skipped, so it produces no line item instead of the previous `NaN`-priced charge; entitlement/priced dimensions behave exactly as before.

Note: I also fixed a pre-existing off-by-one in `DatetimeUtils.randomTimeAndDateLastMonth` (day `0` resolved to the month *before* last), which made `offeringPackage.entity.spec.ts` "FTPCOP-5" fail ~1 run in 25 on the untouched baseline.
